blanks.sentence: For one family, eating together was often the _____ when everyone could meet and chat.
blanks.section: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — Family meals

blanks.sentence: Eating with close family members brought a sense of _____.
In a different group, someone known as the funny one may instead become the _____.
In the past, children were sometimes seated at a _____ from adults.
One mother's children were not brought up being _____ from adults at meals.

multipleChoice.question: What does the family-meal example suggest about the children?
options: They find it easier to discuss their day and concerns while eating.
They usually save their questions until the meal has finished.
They prefer to discuss difficult matters with people outside the family.
They talk most freely when the family follows a formal routine.

multipleChoice.question: What does the example of moving to another group suggest about family roles?
options: A person's role depends mainly on how long the group has known them.
A person should adopt the same role in every group they join.
A person's usual family label may not describe them in every group.
A person needs another group to discover their true family role.

multipleChoice.question: How does this mother's approach differ from the older dinner-table arrangements described?
options: It gives children a separate space to discuss their own concerns.
It makes age the basis for deciding who may join a discussion.
It leaves adults to raise difficult subjects on the children's behalf.
It lets children ask questions across the former adult–child divide.

multipleChoice.question: What can be inferred about the older generation's response to the children's questions?
options: They oppose the children's questions despite enjoying family meals.
They are largely favourable, although the freedom to ask is unfamiliar.
They feel comfortable because the children follow old table rules.
They approve only when the children sit at a separate table.
